# 1 Enoch Chapter 90 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Dreams — Animal Apocalypse

---

**1** And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.

**2** And I saw until horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw until there sprouted a great horn of one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.

**3** And it looked at them and their eyes opened, and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.

**4** And notwithstanding all this those eagles and vultures and ravens and kites still kept tearing the sheep and swooping down upon them and devouring them: still the sheep remained silent, but the rams lamented and cried out.

**5** And those ravens fought and battled with it and sought to lay low its horn, but they had no power over it.

**6** And I saw until the shepherds and eagles and those vultures and kites came, and they cried to the ravens that they should break the horn of that ram, and they battled and fought with it, and it fought with them and cried out that its help might come.

**7** And I saw until that man who wrote down the names of the shepherds and carried up the book to the Lord of the sheep came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down for the help of that ram.

**8** And I saw until the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled and they all fell into His shadow from before His face.

**9** All the eagles and vultures and ravens and kites were gathered together, and there came with them all the sheep of the field; yea, they all came together and helped each other to break that horn of the ram.

**10** And I saw that man, who wrote the book according to the command of the Lord, until he opened that book concerning the destruction which those twelve last shepherds had wrought, and showed that they had destroyed much more than their predecessors, before the Lord of the sheep.

**11** And I saw until the Lord of the sheep came to them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from the midst of those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.

**12** And I saw until a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep proceeded against all the beasts of the field to slay them, and all the beasts and the birds of the heaven fled before their face.

**13** And I saw that man sitting on a lofty throne of judgment and the books of the living were opened before Him, and all His host and His whole court stood before Him, and the hearts of all were filled with joy because that man had been protected and written therein.

**14** And I saw until those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty and cast into that fiery abyss.

**15** And I saw that man cast into an abyss, full of fire, flaming and full of pillars of fire; and those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty and cast into that fiery abyss.

**16** And I saw at that time how a like abyss was opened in the midst of the earth, full of fire, and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and cast into this fiery abyss, and they burned; now this abyss was to the right of that house.

**17** And I saw those sheep burning and their bones burning.

**18** And I stood up to see until they folded up that old house; and carried off all the pillars, and all the beams and ornaments of the house were at the same time folded up with it, and they carried it off and laid it in a place in the south of the land.

**19** And I saw until the Lord of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.

**20** And I saw all the sheep which had been left, and all the beasts on the earth, and all the birds of the heaven, falling down and doing homage to those sheep and making petition to and obeying them in everything.

**21** And thereafter those three who were clothed in white and had seized me by my hand who had taken me up before, and the hand of that ram also seizing hold of me, they took me up and set me down in the midst of those sheep before the judgment took place.

**22** And those sheep were all white, and their wool was abundant and clean.

**23** And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.

**24** And I saw until they laid down that sword, which had been given to the sheep, and they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed before the presence of the Lord; and all the sheep were invited into that house, but it held them not.

**25** And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them that did not see.

**26** And I saw that that house was large and broad and very full.

**27** And I saw that a white bull was born, with large horns and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and made petition to him all the time.

**28** And I saw until all their generations were transformed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb, and that lamb became a great animal and had great black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the oxen.

**29** And I slept in their midst: and I awoke and saw everything.

**30** This is the vision which I saw while I slept, and I awoke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory.

**31** Then I wept with a great weeping and my tears stayed not until I could no longer endure it: when I saw, they flowed on account of what I had seen; for everything shall come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men in their order were shown to me.

**32** On that night I remembered the first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled because I had seen that vision.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Ge'ez text. Chapter 90 climaxes with: (1) the Maccabean revolt (lambs with horns, great horn = Judas Maccabeus); (2) the final divine judgment (Lord strikes earth, opens books, condemns 70 shepherds, burns apostate sheep); (3) the new house = the New Jerusalem; (4) the white bull = the Messiah; (5) the transformation of all into white bulls = eschatological restoration. The vision concludes with Enoch weeping (v. 31-32) — the weight of witnessing the whole of history.*
